companyDescription: US critical minerals · 19% of ReElement Technologies, which just took $25M from the Dept of War to build domestic rare-earth refining at Marion, Indiana
priceNote: Live price Aug 13 07:49, -3.45% today. Prior report (Aug 4) used $2.21 — +26.7% drift in 9 days. That run is why the Base scenario has been re-derived: the target price is unchanged at $4.20, but from $2.80 that is +50%, not the +90% the stale report was still advertising.
sector: Materials / Critical Minerals & Rare Earth Elements
summary: The thesis got better and the entry got worse, which is the whole reason this refresh exists. ReElement Technologies — AREC holds 19% — secured a $25M US Department of War investment to expand domestic critical-mineral and rare-earth refining, lifted planned capacity to over 16,000 metric tons from roughly 8,000, and is targeting initial germanium production in Q3 2026 at its Marion, Indiana campus. AREC also secured a $200M equity facility, holds $72.5M cash, is paying a special dividend of $0.0431/share, and joins the Russell 3000 and Microcap indexes at reconstitution. But the stock has run 26.7% since the last report, so the same $4.20 Base target is now +50% rather than +90% — the board was ranking this pick #3 on upside it had already spent. No analyst price targets were locatable at write time, so every scenario here is thesis-derived, not consensus-anchored.

risks: Entry is 26.7% worse than nine days ago — same target, far less remaining upside, and this is the pick the board most over-ranked
No analyst coverage found at write time, so there is no external check on any of these scenarios — they are thesis-derived and should carry less weight than a consensus-anchored pick
Exposure is indirect: AREC owns 19% of ReElement, so the rare-earth story accrues to shareholders at a fraction, not one-for-one
A $200M equity facility on a ~$300M market cap is a standing dilution overhang — drawing it is how this thesis gets funded and how holders get diluted
Germanium production start is a target, not a committed date; slipping past Q3 removes the only near-dated operational milestone
Critical-minerals policy support is real but politically contingent; the Dept of War money is a program, not a contract

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed funds 3.50-3.75%, held Jul 29 with three dissents for a hike. Next FOMC Sep 16.
macroRisk.inflationNote: July CPI (Aug 12) headline 3.4% from 3.5%, core 2.5%, +0.1% m/m — soft print after payrolls at -23k.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: A ~$300M pre-scale miner funding a refining build-out is about as rate-sensitive as equities get: the $200M facility prices off risk appetite, not fundamentals. Offsetting that, critical-minerals policy funding is fiscal rather than monetary, so the Dept of War money doesn't care what the Fed does.

postLose.note: AREC gave back only -1.69% on an Aug 2026 disappointment, but that was against a much lower base. Having now run 26.7%, the give-back on a germanium slip is far larger than the historical average suggests.

spotSizing.reason: Held at 4%, inside the turbo lane's 2-5% strict maximum. The Dept of War investment and $72.5M cash genuinely reduce failure risk, but a 26.7% worse entry and zero analyst coverage offset that — improved fundamentals never buy more than the 5% ceiling in this lane.
